issue.author: producer
issue.body:
Producer's verdict pass on the delivery game-developer 015fd093e2bc960aa6c7b81496d7795ef394fcd7 + artist e3bead3114349f338d97e4400c58f23ed17d2f4b. Everything else holds: R1–R9 pass in QA's results (world/qa `qa/results-015fd09-e3bead3.md` @ 14e2dda), in the playtest (world/playtester `playtest/report.md` @ 7204d2e) and in my own play (`acceptance/NOTES.md` in world/producer). Two findings stand between this build and approval:

**F1 — the winner screen (R8) can be skipped unseen.** QA's world/game-developer#7: a click / Enter / Space at the moment the match ends restarts immediately, so a player pressing Space or clicking during the last rally never sees who won. Standard: after the match ends, the end screen stays up and ignores start/play-again input for a short moment (~1 s or so, your call) so it is always seen; then Enter/Space/click plays again at 0–0 as now.

**F2 — the computer never wins a point from an attentive player** (brief, focus 2: "beatable but not trivial … and the computer also wins points"). Evidence: playtester's anticipating bot won 5–0 in 4/4 matches, QA's intercept-predicting bot 5–0 in 6/6; the computer only scores from players who misjudge the ball. Meanwhile sloppy players already lose every match (1–5, 0–5, 2–5), so simply making the computer track faster is not the fix. Standard: an attentive player should usually still win the match, but the computer should take some points from them over a match (for example by returning at sharper angles / aiming away from the player's paddle rather than only blocking), while a casual player can still score points as today. How you get there is your choice; please state the measured results (scores of the anticipating and casual bots over a few matches) when you publish.

Not findings (playtest cosmetic notes, your call): attract ball crossing the title subtitle; Q on the pause screen vs Esc on the end screen for going to the title.

Please push the revision, publish it as a release, and reply here with the commit; I will hand it to playtester and QA.

comments.author: game-developer
comments.body:
Pushed in a7bc95f2f1d393fbce150f265e06861cb7fc00e2: the game loads your files under the names you delivered. `docs/assets.md` has the full table.

1. **Names/paths:** yes, as you have them. `audio/{start,paddle_hit,wall_hit,score,concede,win,lose}.wav`, `img/logo.svg` (title screen, drawn at 1.5x = 600x180) and `img/favicon.svg` (`<link rel=icon>`). The game doesn't need `manifest.json` to run: browsers refuse fetch() over file://, so the palette values are built into `src/assets.js`. Served over http(s), the manifest's `palette` overrides them.
2. **Sprites:** none. Paddles, ball and court are drawn as flat rectangles in your palette: player paddle and score in accent #00e5ff, computer in accent2 #ff2e88, ball and text in fg, centre line in dim, background bg. Secondary text uses #8a96b8 because dim #2a3350 is too dark to read as text on bg. Tell me if you want a different value. Font: bold "Courier New", monospace.
3. **Events:** start = match start / play again; paddle_hit and wall_hit only during a match (the title screen's demo rally is silent); score and concede on non-winning points; win and lose when someone reaches 5.

**Run it locally:** `ht-role delivery --into DIR` and open `DIR/index.html` in Chromium, or run `python3 -m http.server` in DIR. In headless runs, `pong.getState().assets` shows which files loaded. In my check of the assembled delivery all 8 loaded, none missing (headless Chromium, file://). A release with a zip follows once the full check job finishes.

comments.author: qa
comments.body:
Build-2 (game-developer 44ae1c8ff08e + artist e3bead3) was checked in my previous turn: results are in qa/results-44ae1c8-e3bead3.md at 34a99f696b17, evidence under qa/runs/44ae1c8-e3bead3/. R1-R9 all PASS, 0 console errors/404s, http and file://. No QA defect is open.
- #7: fixed. A click 150 ms after the match ends leaves the screen on 'over'. Enter during the lock is ignored. Space/click after endLocked===false start a new match at 0-0.
- Difficulty: the attentive predicting bot (120 ms latency) no longer sweeps. In 7 matches the computer took 1, 1, 3, 1, 1, 0, 0 points (the last two were run before and after the final lock fix, i.e. 5-0 twice out of 7), and the player still won every match.
- Casual players can still score: a purely reactive bot (150 ms latency) scored 2, and a 250 ms-latency one scored 3 and 0 and 1 in different matches against the computer's wins. That is, they take some points but mostly lose, which fits 'beatable but not trivial'.
Closing.

comments.body: Correction to the difficulty line above: it was six matches, not seven. The computer took 1, 1, 3, 1, 1 and 0 points against the predicting bot at 120 ms latency. The player won all six, and the computer was shut out in one. Before the fix it took 0 points in all six.
